# Release Gate Checklist: TeamPulse Work Intake and Tracking

**Purpose**: Formal requirements-quality release gate covering authorization, workflow, auditability, performance, reliability, and recovery expectations.
**Created**: 2026-08-24
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact for product, engineering, security, QA, and release reviewers. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 - Are all request lifecycle states, valid transitions, terminal behavior, and transition guards explicitly defined? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK002 - Are permissions defined for every supported role across creation, visibility, status, priority, ownership, and category actions? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004, §FR-007, §FR-013]
- [x] CHK003 - Are all important audit event types, recorded values, actor information, timestamps, reasons, retention, and immutability requirements specified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006, §FR-014]
- [x] CHK004 - Are the request creation rules explicit about required fields, initial status, assignment timing, and valid enum values? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002, §FR-003]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK005 - Is the term “authorized user” replaced or supplemented with clear actor, action, resource, and scope conditions? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001, §FR-007]
- [x] CHK006 - Are the `requester`, `assignee`, `team_lead`, `approver`, and `admin` roles defined consistently across the specification and authorization policy? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013]
- [x] CHK007 - Is the distinction between assigning an owner and changing request status clear, including the rule for an open request becoming assigned? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004, §FR-008]
- [x] CHK008 - Is “priority” defined with an approved value set and an unambiguous interpretation for engineering work? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK009 - Are lifecycle rules consistent between the user stories, functional requirements, data model, API contract, and implementation plan? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK010 - Are priority permissions consistent for team leads, approvers, admins, and all other roles across every artifact? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005, §FR-013]
- [x] CHK011 - Are request visibility rules consistent with the stated single-team scope and role boundaries? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007, Assumptions]
- [x] CHK012 - Do audit requirements consistently include status, priority, assignee, and category changes without omitting any declared important event? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006, §FR-014]

## Authorization and Security Requirements

- [x] CHK013 - Are authentication assumptions, trusted identity inputs, and required identity attributes defined for every protected API operation? [Completeness, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK014 - Are deny-by-default behavior and unauthorized response semantics defined for creation, visibility, status, priority, ownership, category, and history access? [Security, Spec §FR-007]
- [x] CHK015 - Are cross-request and cross-user access boundaries explicitly defined so request history cannot expose unrelated internal details? [Security, Spec §FR-012]
- [x] CHK016 - Are administrator overrides constrained by explicit authorization, reason capture, and audit requirements? [Security, Spec §FR-007, §FR-014]

## Workflow and Auditability Requirements

- [x] CHK017 - Are shortcut, backward, duplicate, and terminal-state transitions explicitly addressed rather than left to implementation interpretation? [Coverage, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK018 - Are assignment and reassignment rules defined for valid owners, ownership conflicts, and the resulting lifecycle state? [Coverage, Spec §FR-004]
- [x] CHK019 - Are requirements clear about which old and new values are retained for each status, priority, assignee, and category event? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, §FR-014]
- [x] CHK020 - Are atomicity and failure requirements defined so a request mutation cannot succeed without its required audit event? [Reliability, Spec §FR-006, §FR-014]
- [x] CHK021 - Are append-only audit behavior and the absence of update/delete paths stated as requirements rather than implementation assumptions? [Completeness, Spec §FR-014]

## Acceptance and Measurement Quality

- [x] CHK022 - Can each authorization rule be objectively evaluated using a defined actor, action, resource, context, expected result, and error outcome? [Measurability, Spec §FR-007, §FR-013]
- [x] CHK023 - Can each lifecycle transition requirement be objectively evaluated with a defined starting state, requested state, guard, and rejection behavior? [Measurability, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK024 - Is the 500 ms p95 target tied to named request-list and request-history operations, normal local load, and a defined measurement window? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006]
- [x] CHK025 - Are the success criteria distinguishable from post-launch business outcomes and linked to observable product or service evidence? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-001, §SC-002, §SC-003, §SC-004, §SC-005]

## Reliability, Recovery, and Operational Requirements

- [x] CHK026 - Are expected behaviors defined for database failures, audit-write failures, transaction rollback, and retry or recovery decisions? [Recovery, Spec §FR-014]
- [x] CHK027 - Are requirements defined for concurrent updates to the same request, including conflict detection and which change is retained? [Edge Case, Gap]
- [x] CHK028 - Are availability, backup, data-loss, and local recovery expectations explicitly included or intentionally excluded for the SQLite deployment scope? [Non-Functional, Gap]
- [x] CHK029 - Are observability requirements defined for denied authorization attempts, invalid transitions, failed mutations, and audit persistence failures? [Non-Functional, Gap]

## API and Compatibility Requirements

- [x] CHK030 - Are endpoint paths, request and response shapes, envelopes, validation rules, and error semantics consistent across all documented operations? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002, §FR-006]
- [x] CHK031 - Is the `/api/v1/` compatibility boundary explicit for every endpoint, including the category and history operations? [Completeness, Gap]
- [x] CHK032 - Are backward-incompatible changes, migration notes, compatibility tests, deprecation periods, and rollback or adoption paths required by the API contract? [Dependency, Constitution Principle VII]
- [x] CHK033 - Are API requirements defined for malformed payloads, unknown requests, unauthorized resources, invalid transitions, duplicate updates, and persistence failures? [Coverage, Spec §FR-007, §FR-008]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [x] CHK034 - Are the hosting environment’s authentication and role-provisioning responsibilities documented with a clear boundary for TeamPulse? [Dependency, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK035 - Are SQLite limitations and the single-team operating scope reflected in requirements for scale, concurrency, and recovery? [Assumption, Plan Technical Context]
- [x] CHK036 - Are all implementation tasks traceable to a user story, functional requirement, measurable outcome, or constitution principle? [Traceability, Plan Project Structure]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- This checklist is a formal requirements release gate and is distinct from `checklists/requirements.md` and `checklists/workflow-governance.md`.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference.
